summary: A cost-optimisation config change to portfolio-service (cfg-2207) shrank its HikariCP JDBC pool from 50 to 5 connections at 09:52:13. With steady request load (~565 req/s, unchanged), the 5-connection pool immediately saturated (total=5, active=5, idle=0, 25-57 threads waiting). GET /v1/portfolio/holdings began failing at 09:53:19 with 'could not acquire JDBC connection', calls blocked ~3s and breached the gateway timeout, producing 504s at api-gateway and the observed p99 spike. The gateway deploy (dep-5220, HTTP/2 to upstreams, 08:00) is a red herring: it preceded onset by ~110 minutes; latency was normal all morning until 09:50; the gateway is not saturated (CPU ~42%); and order-service, which received the same HTTP/2 upstream change and shares ledger-db, is completely unaffected. The DB itself is healthy (CPU ~30%, slow queries flat, connections_active normal). Root cause: config_change in portfolio-service.

ranked_hypotheses.title: portfolio-service JDBC pool shrunk to 5 by cost-optimisation config, saturating under normal load
ranked_hypotheses.statement: Config change cfg-2207 set portfolio-service db.pool.max_size=5 (from 50) at 09:52:13. With unchanged demand (~565 req/s) the 5-connection Hikari pool instantly saturated (total=5, active=5, idle=0, waiting 25-57), so /v1/portfolio/holdings requests blocked ~3s on connection acquire and failed; upstream calls timed out at api-gateway, producing p99 >4s and 504s.

causal_chain.claim: pool instantly capped at 5 -> db_pool_in_use flat 5.0
normal request load saturates 5 connections -> 3s acquire timeouts

assumptions: No other portfolio-service change occurred at 09:52 (only cfg-2207 appears in the config-change feed for the window).
The 5-connection pool was genuinely insufficient for the steady ~565 req/s / ~12-connection working set.

ranked_hypotheses.title: api-gateway dep-5220 HTTP/2-to-upstream upgrade caused the timeouts
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The api-gateway v9.3.0 deploy (dep-5220, HTTP/2 to portfolio-service/order-service upstreams, 08:00) broke or degraded upstream handling, causing 504s on /v1/portfolio/*.

causal_chain.claim: dep-5220 enables h2 to portfolio-service at 08:00
upstream requests time out at gateway

assumptions: The gateway deploy could cause latent, delayed failures only for portfolio-service.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Timing and scope both refute it: onset is 09:50-09:53, ~110 min after the 08:00 deploy, with normal gateway latency 08:00-09:40 (F1). The gateway is not saturated (CPU ~42%, F13). order-service got the same h2 change (F3) and the same shared ledger-db and is unaffected (F11). The failures are localized to portfolio-service's own JDBC pool, whose cap changed exactly at onset (F4,F6,F7).

ranked_hypotheses.title: ledger-db (shared database) degradation
ranked_hypotheses.statement: ledger-db slowed or refused connections, causing portfolio-service (and the gateway via it) to time out.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: ledger-db metrics are entirely flat/healthy (CPU ~30%, slow queries ~1/min, connections_active normal, F12) and order-service querying the same DB is unaffected (F11).

ranked_hypotheses.title: Capacity saturation from organic load growth
ranked_hypotheses.statement: Traffic outgrew provisioned capacity, exhausting connections.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: request_rate is flat ~558-586 req/s across onset (F8); pool size was deliberately reduced 50->5 (F4), not outgrown.

facts.statement: api-gateway p99 latency was normal (~207ms) through 09:40, then spiked to ~3120ms at 09:50 and ~4300ms afterward.
cfg-2207 changed portfolio-service db.pool.max_size from 50 to 5 at 09:52:00Z.
portfolio-service logged 'config change cfg-2207 applied: db.pool.max_size=5' at 09:52:13Z, then its first connection-acquire failure 66s later at 09:53:19Z.
portfolio-service Hikari pool sat at total=5, active=5, idle=0 with 25-57 threads waiting.
portfolio-service db_pool_in_use fell from ~12 to a flat 5.0 after the change.
portfolio-service request_rate was flat ~565 req/s across the onset, ruling out load growth.
order-service, which received the same HTTP/2 upstream change and shares ledger-db, stayed flat at ~150ms p99.
ledger-db was healthy (CPU ~30%, slow queries ~1/min, connections_active normal).
api-gateway CPU stayed flat at ~42%, so the gateway itself was not saturated.
portfolio-service's other deps (market-data-service ~40ms p99, redis-cache ~22% CPU) were healthy.
A near-identical past incident (HIST-115) was a datasource pool size overridden by a wrong environment profile.

assumptions: The config-change feed for the window is complete (get_config_changes returned count=2 for all services, count=0 for portfolio-service after 11:00), so cfg-2207 is the only portfolio-service change near onset.
The reported 'gateway upgrade' (dep-5220) is the change the reporter suspected, and it is the only api-gateway deployment in the window.
portfolio-service's 3s acquire timeout is shorter than api-gateway's upstream timeout, so gateway-side 504s are a consequence rather than the origin.

timeline.event: api-gateway v9.3.0 (dep-5220) deployed enabling HTTP/2 to portfolio-service and order-service upstreams; gateway latency stays normal.
Last normal bucket before onset (gateway p99 ~207ms, portfolio p99 ~180ms, error rates ~0.2%).
Onset: portfolio-service and api-gateway latency/error metrics step up sharply.
First 'could not acquire JDBC connection within 3000ms' for GET /v1/portfolio/holdings.
Steady degraded state: portfolio db_pool_in_use pinned at 5.0; both services at elevated latency/error rates through 11:59.

recommended_actions.action: Revert cfg-2207: restore portfolio-service db.pool.max_size to 50 (or a validated value) immediately.
recommended_actions.rationale: Directly removes the fault; H1 attributes the outage to the 50->5 pool shrink at 09:52.

recommended_actions.action: Confirm recovery by watching portfolio-service db_pool_in_use, error_rate and api-gateway p99/504s return to pre-09:50 baselines.
Do NOT roll back dep-5220 on the strength of this incident; the gateway deploy is not the cause.
recommended_actions.rationale: Timing (110 min lead), gateway health, and unaffected order-service all exonerate the deploy.

recommended_actions.action: Add guardrails/validation to the 'small' cost-optimisation profile so datasource pool sizes cannot be reduced below a service's observed concurrency.
recommended_actions.rationale: Matches the historical root cause of HIST-115 (pool overridden by wrong profile).

recommended_actions.action: Alert on config changes that reduce connection-pool max_size and on sustained Hikari 'waiting>0' / pool-in-use pinned at max.
recommended_actions.rationale: Would have flagged the 09:52 change within seconds rather than via user reports.

data_gaps: No direct confirmation that reverting cfg-2207 restores service (not yet attempted in the data window) — causal chain is inferred from timing + exact pool-size coincidence, not a controlled rollback.

Order-of-latency-blocks: 09:50 metric bucket shows a partial step before the 09:52:13 config apply, most consistent with 10-min bucket averaging straddling the onset, but exact second-level onset of the metric step is not resolvable from 10-min buckets.
ledger-db has no latency_p99_ms metric, so DB responsiveness was assessed only via cpu_pct, slow_queries_per_min and connections_active.

findings.statement: api-gateway p99 latency was normal (~205-214ms avg) from 08:00 through 09:40, then jumped to ~3120ms at 09:50 and ~4300ms from 10:00 onward.
api-gateway error_rate rose from ~0.2% to 4.44% at 09:50 and ~7.2% thereafter.
A single deployment dep-5220 (api-gateway v9.3.0) was deployed at 08:00:00Z enabling HTTP/2 to upstreams for portfolio-service and order-service; never rolled back.

findings.statement: Config change cfg-2207 changed portfolio-service db.pool.max_size from 50 to 5 at 09:52:00Z.
portfolio-service logged 'config change cfg-2207 applied: db.pool.max_size=5' at 09:52:13Z, then its first connection-acquire failure at 09:53:19Z.
portfolio-service errored with 'could not acquire JDBC connection' and HikariPool failures showing total=5, active=5, idle=0, waiting=25-57.

findings.statement: portfolio-service db_pool_in_use dropped from ~12 connections before to a flat 5.0 (avg and max) from 10:00 onward.
portfolio-service request_rate stayed flat at ~558-586 req/s across the onset (no load surge).
portfolio-service error_rate jumped from ~0.2% to 13.5% at 09:50 and ~22% thereafter; latency_p99 jumped from ~180ms to ~3031ms at 09:50.
api-gateway flagged the failures as upstream timeouts specifically to portfolio-service: 252 'upstream timeout portfolio-service GET /v1/portfolio/holdings -> 504' WARNs, first at 09:53:53Z.
order-service, which also received the HTTP/2 upstream change and shares ledger-db, was completely unaffected: p99 flat ~148-151ms throughout.
ledger-db was healthy throughout: cpu_pct flat ~30%, slow_queries_per_min flat ~1, connections_active normal (~55-67).
api-gateway CPU stayed flat at ~42% (37-47% range), i.e. the gateway itself was not resource-saturated.
portfolio-service's other dependencies were healthy: market-data-service p99 flat ~40ms; redis-cache CPU flat ~22%.
A past incident HIST-115 has the same signature: 'order-service connection pool misconfiguration' caused by a datasource pool size overridden by a wrong environment profile, category config_change.

findings.statement: The 09:50-09:53 onset is coeval with cfg-2207 (09:52) and the pool cap is exactly 5, so the config change, not the 08:00 gateway deploy, caused the saturation; the gateway 504s are a downstream symptom of portfolio-service's 3s connection-acquire timeouts.
